'''Svetlana Yurievna Zaginaichenko''' ({{langx|uk|Світлана Юріївна Загінайченко}}, {{langx|ru|Светлана Юрьевна Загинайченко}}; 10 August 1957 - 23 November 2015) was a Ukrainian [[Solid-state physics|solid state]] physicist. She studied the physical properties of carbon materials and their application to [[hydrogen energy storage]]. She was a nominee for the 2016 [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] for her work in studying [[fullerene]]s.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Загінайченко Світлана Юріївна — Енциклопедія Сучасної України |url=https://esu.com.ua/search_articles.php?id=15156 |access-date=2022-03-30 |website=esu.com.ua| isbn=9789660220744 }}</ref>

== Education ==
Zaginaichenko earned a physics degree with honors from [[Oles Honchar Dnipro National University]] in 1979.<ref name=":0">''Загинайченко С.Ю., Матысина З.А., Щур Д.В., Джавадов Н.Ф.'' Статистическая теория фуллеритов и особенности их практического использования / Щур Д.В.. — Научная монография посвящена памяти Светланы Юрьевны Загинайченко. — Киев : «КИМ», 2016. — С. I—IV. — 486 с.</ref>

In 1984, Zaginaichenko defended her dissertation on the physical properties of hexagonally-structured and [[Interstitial compound|interstitial alloys]] at [[National Metallurgical Academy of Ukraine|Dnipro Metallurgical Institute]], earning the degree of [[Candidate of Science|Candidate of Physical and Mathematical Sciences]] (which is the [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] equivalent of a [[Doctor of Philosophy]]).<ref>''Загинайченко Светлана Юрьевна.'' Растворимость, магнетизм и перераспределение атомов в упорядочивающихся сплавах гексагональных структур / проф.,д.ф-м.н. Воробьев Г.М.. — Ученая cтепень: кандидат физико-математических наук. — Днепропетровск : Минестерство высшего и среднего образования СССР Днепропетровский металургический институт имени Л. И. Брежнева, 1984. — 192 с.</ref> Her thesis focused on [[Hexagonal Close-Packed|hexagonal close-packed]] structures and developed theories for [[impurity]] [[solubility]], interstitial atom [[Kinetics (physics)|kinetics]], and [[magnetism]] of such alloys.[[File:Zaginaichenko S.Yu. Plaque.jpg|thumb|A memorial plaque commemorating Zaginaichenko's life, located on the house in Dnipro where she grew up.]]

== Career ==
From 4 November 1995 until her death in 2015, Zaginaichenko was a leading researcher at the Department for Hydrogen Materials and Carbon Nanostructures at the Institute for Problems of Materials Sciences at the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute for Problems of Materials Sciences National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine |url=https://www.nas.gov.ua/EN/Org/Pages/default.aspx?OrgID=0000298 |access-date=2022-03-30 |website=www.nas.gov.ua |language=uk-UA}}</ref> She was one of the founding members of the Association of Hydrogen Energy in Ukraine (AHEU), which was formed with the support of [[Turhan Nejat Veziroğlu|Turhan Nejat Veziroglu]], the president of the International Association of Hydrogen Energy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ассоциация Водородной Энергетики в Украине |url=http://www.aheu.com.ua/about.html |access-date=2022-03-30 |website=www.aheu.com.ua}}</ref> She was also part of the organizing committee for the International Conference of Carbon Nanomaterials in Clean Energy Hydrogen Systems.<ref>{{Cite web |title=XII International Conference CARBON NANOMATERIALS Hydrogen Systems |url=http://aheu.com.ua/ichms10.html |access-date=2022-03-30 |website=aheu.com.ua |language=ru}}</ref>

She was nominated for the 2016 Nobel Prize in Chemistry<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-03-21 |title="Исследование процессов и систем водородного и гелиоводородного преобразования энергии" |url=http://www.lab67.kiev.ua/Itogi2015/itogi2015.html |access-date=2022-03-31 |website= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321063834/http://www.lab67.kiev.ua/Itogi2015/itogi2015.html |archive-date=21 March 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref> for her work in studying the physical structure of fullerenes and proving that they have three main configurations<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Schur |first1=D. V. |last2=Zaginaichenko |first2=S. Y. |last3=Veziroglu |first3=T. N. |date=2015-02-19 |title=The hydrogenation process as a method of investigation of fullerene C60 molecule |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319914034892 |journal=International Journal of Hydrogen Energy |language=en |volume=40 |issue=6 |pages=2742–2762 |doi=10.1016/j.ijhydene.2014.12.092 |issn=0360-3199|url-access=subscription }}</ref> ([[isomer]]s). However, she died before the 2016 announcement of the prize, so even if the prize committee had chosen to honor this contribution, the prize's rules against posthumous awards would have prevented her from winning it.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/europe/five-things-to-know-about-the-nobel-prizes/articleshow/86744459.cms|newspaper=Times of India|title=Five things to know about the Nobel prizes|date=October 4, 2021}}</ref>
